L160's declared-but-unconsumed gates), recorded because it reads as a discovery to whoever finds it next. Three occurrences, no writer and no reader: (1) the string table; (2) the static key list feeding spawnEnvKeys(), which builds a SET OF KEY NAMES to carry/diff for shell snapshots and does not assign values; (3) `var JTn="CLAUDE_CODE_INVOKED_SKILLS"` in the shell-snapshot chunk, whose sole occurrence is its own declaration -- the neighbouring Ake() wrapper-builder uses only Pke (CLAUDE_CODE_EXECPATH). It is NOT set by Fke(), the Bash/hook child env builder. WHY IT MATTERS: it is the obvious name to reach for when asking 'can a shell learn which skill/plugin is executing', and the answer today is NO -- there is no first-party channel; the model knows the path it read a file at and nothing else does. The adjacent ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR} is likewise not an env var but a substitution token replaced into skill DEFINITION text at load (which is where the 'Base directory for this skill:' prefix comes from). Identity therefore travels via the model passing what it already knows, not via the environment. Surfaced by the creative-problem-solving project asking whether a shell-side identity channel exists.

entries.name: CLAUDE_ENV_FILE
entries.summary: DESIGNED channel for a hook to inject environment into subsequent Bash tool calls. Set for FOUR hook events -- SessionStart, Setup, CwdChanged, FileChanged (verified in the hook executor: if(!Ie && (t==="SessionStart"||t==="Setup"||t==="CwdChanged"||t==="FileChanged") && x!==void 0) tt.CLAUDE_ENV_FILE=await _2e(t,x)) -- though only the CwdChanged and FileChanged descriptions say so out loud. NOT LAST-WRITER-WINS IN A RACY SENSE: the loader CONCATENATES the per-hook scripts in a fixed order (setup=0, sessionstart=1, cwdchanged=2, filechanged=3, then hook index) and joins them into one script, so the final `export` wins TEXTUALLY and the winner is reproducible from the install set alone. NOTE (corrected 2026-08-29): this entry previously cited 'two independent machines with the same plugins observed the identical leaked pair' as corroboration. They were two agent SESSIONS ON ONE MACHINE, and the mechanism described in this very sentence is why that observation could never have been independent -- a deterministic winner computed from a shared install set will of course be identical in every session on that install. The determinism is the finding; the second sighting added nothing. Set for the CwdChanged and FileChanged hook events, whose own descriptions say verbatim: 'CLAUDE_ENV_FILE is set -- write bash exports there to apply env to subsequent BashTool commands.' Loader messages: 'Session environment loaded from CLAUDE_ENV_FILE', 'Session environment loaded from N hook file(s)', 'Session environment script ready (N chars total)', 'No session environment scripts found', 'Failed to clear cwd env files'. CONSEQUENCE: the Bash tool's environment is NOT just {inherited + Fke()} -- hooks can add to it, so a variable's presence in a Bash call does not imply the runtime set it for that call. This is the mechanism behind CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT appearing in a shell pointing at an unrelated plugin (see env.CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT). LANE NOTE: this is a plain-CLI mechanism; under Cowork the VM shell is sealed and hook exports do NOT cross the host/VM boundary (Ch30/L116), so the published Cowork guidance 'do not use a hook to export env for your shell commands' remains correct for that lane and is NOT contradicted here.

entries.name: CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT
entries.summary: ANSWER FIRST -- how a skill reaches its own bundled scripts, shell-side: (1) ship a launcher in the plugin's bin/ and call it as a BARE COMMAND (see tool.plugin_bin_on_path) -- Claude Code puts <plugin>/bin on the Bash tool's PATH with a path correct for that shell's namespace in every lane measured, so nothing crosses the boundary; (2) if the launcher is absent, DISCOVER the directory shell-side and verify with a sentinel file; (3) NEVER read $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT in a shell -- it is frequently SET, to an unrelated plugin's directory (see below), so it fails as a confident wrong answer rather than an empty one; (4) ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} written into a SKILL.md or command BODY is substituted at load and is fine for a FILE-TOOL read -- it is only shell use and runtime-read reference files that break. MECHANISM AND PROVENANCE FOLLOW. PRECISION (2026-08-28, vs CLI 2.1.250 + Desktop app.asar 1.37937.3): this is TWO mechanisms and the distinction is load-bearing. (A) SUBSTITUTION TOKEN -- ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} is text-replaced into plugin-declared definition strings (hook commands, MCP command/args, Monitor commands, permission-rule prefixes) before execution. (B) OUTBOUND ENV VAR into THREE child spawns only: plugin-declared command spawns, MCP stdio servers, and an MCP headersHelper exec env. CORRECTED 2026-08-29 (was: 'NOT set on the agent's own process environment, so it does NOT reach the Bash tool'). Fke(), the Bash child-env builder, still adds no plugin root -- that part stands. But the Bash env is {...xa() (INHERITED process env), ...} and there is a DESIGNED channel that writes into it: CLAUDE_ENV_FILE. The CwdChanged and FileChanged hook descriptions say verbatim 'CLAUDE_ENV_FILE is set -- write bash exports there to apply env to subsequent BashTool commands', and the loader logs 'Session environment loaded from CLAUDE_ENV_FILE' / 'loaded from N hook file(s)'. Since the HOOK EXECUTOR sets CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT into each hook's own spawn env, a hook that exports its environment leaks ITS plugin's root into the session env for every later Bash call. MEASURED in two agent sessions ON THE SAME MACHINE (corrected 2026-08-29 -- previously written as 'two independent machines/sessions'; they share a host and filesystem, and per env.CLAUDE_ENV_FILE the winning export is deterministic from the shared install set, so the second sighting was not independent corroboration and the pair would be identical in any session on this install): the Bash tool saw CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT=<.../lool-founder-skills/founder-skills/0.7.1> and CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA=<.../data/codex-openai-codex> -- two DIFFERENT plugins, NEITHER being the plugin whose skill was running. So the shell-side failure mode is NOT 'silently empty' but 'silently set to an unrelated plugin's directory', which is worse: a confident wrong answer instead of an obviously missing one. The operational rule is unchanged and strengthened: NEVER read $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT in a shell -- you may get nothing, or someone else's plugin. Prefer tool.plugin_bin_on_path. Credit: disputed and measured by the skill-creator-plus session; mechanism traced here. Verified: the Bash child env is {...xa() (inherited process env), SHELL, GIT_EDITOR, ...envOverrides, ...sandboxEnv, ...Fke(), ...unset} -- it DOES inherit process env, so the var would pass through if it were there, and it is not; Fke() adds no plugin root. env.CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT has ZERO read sites. COUNTS CORRECTED 2026-08-29, and the first correction was itself wrong. Published numbers were 'all three occurrences' (asar) and 59 (CLI). A first pass 'corrected' these to 9 and 56, calling 56 byte-level truth and 59 a null-stripping artifact. TRUE VALUES: asar 1.40609.0 = 9 (ASCII 9 + UTF-16LE 0); CLI 2.1.250 = 59 (ASCII 56 + UTF-16LE 3). THE ORIGINAL 59 WAS RIGHT. Three instruments, three distinct failures: (a) grep -c counts LINES and these artifacts are effectively one line -- it under-reported the asar as 3 (real error, correction stands); (b) an ASCII-only raw-byte regex CANNOT SEE UTF-16LE-stored strings -- it under-reported the CLI as 56; (c) a null-stripped extract (tr -d '\000') does NOT fabricate matches, it DECODES UTF-16LE (each ASCII char followed by \x00), which is why it found 59 -- 56+3=59 exactly. Rule: count in BOTH encodings, or state which one you counted; never call an ASCII count 'byte-level truth'. The three UTF-16LE sites are prose (a changelog line about literal ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} in hook errors, and the Monitor tool description twice). NONE of the 9 assigns into the agent's process environment. CONSEQUENCE, and a correction to how this entry previously read: the note that 'bash ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/x.sh works' under VM-loop is about a HOOK COMMAND STRING being substituted before execution -- NOT about a model-issued Bash call being able to read $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT, which it cannot, on any surface checked. A skill needing its own root shell-side should prefer a bin/ LAUNCHER -- see tool.plugin_bin_on_path, the one measured channel that resolves in the SHELL's namespace -- and fall back to discovery. Under Cowork the Desktop picks the dir per mode: Ei = isHostLoopModeEnabled ? qX(installPath) : sdkPath. Host-loop => host-side path, accepted by host file tools but unreachable from in-VM bash, which must use the VM mount instead; VM-loop => sdkPath = that VM mount. Decisive: claude-hostloop-plugins is absent from both agent binaries (host CLI 2.1.201, in-VM ELF 2.1.197), present only in app.asar, so L89's 'host-side EVERYWHERE' is host-loop-only. Host-loop qX mechanics, re-confirmed at 1.37937.3: space-triggered (returns the raw install path unless it contains a space) and deterministic (sha256(installPath).slice(0,16), stable across invocations/sessions/reboots). Host-loop mechanics live-confirmed 2026-07-07 via docs/internal/cowork-pluginroot-probe; VM-loop resolution static-derived from the branch. VM MOUNT SHAPES re-derived at 1.37937.3: remote => /sessions/<id>/mnt/.remote-plugins/<plugin id> (tail is exactly the plugin id, so a file-tool-path basename joins the two namespaces); local => /sessions/<id>/mnt/.local-plugins/<guestCompatibleRelative(accountOrgRoot, installPath)> -- a relative-path MIRROR of the host layout, NOT a fixed cache/<marketplace>/<plugin>/<version> depth. Mount-level constants are .auto-memory/.remote-plugins/.local-plugins (plus non-plugin .claude/.projects/uploads/outputs). TRAP: skills are ALSO advertised at /sessions/<id>/mnt/.claude/<...>/<sanitizeSkillName(name)>, which is a SKILL mount and does not contain the plugin's scripts/ -- a name-matched search can succeed there and still be wrong, so match on a sentinel file, never a directory name.

entries.name: CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR
entries.summary: ANSWER FIRST: `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}` is a SKILL.md-BODY-TEXT feature, not an environment variable. Use it to point a FILE TOOL at a bundled file. Never use it in a shell command -- it is not exported, so it expands to the empty string and the command silently addresses a path at the filesystem root. To run a bundled script from a shell, ship a launcher in the plugin's `bin/` and call it as a bare command (see tool.plugin_bin_on_path), or have the model pass an absolute path it already resolved. MECHANISM (first-party, CLI 2.1.250): every site is a literal string replacement -- `.replace(/\$\{CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR\}/g, ...)` and `.replaceAll("${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}", ...)` -- carrying the same THREE LIMITS as env.CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT: (1) substitution, not environment; (2) BRACED FORM ONLY -- `$CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR` matches no pattern and passes through untouched; (3) DEFINITION TEXT ONLY, and only when the skill owns a directory -- the sites are getPromptForCommand's body text and the `allowed-tools` frontmatter, both gated on a resolved skill root (isSkillMode / non-null baseDir); where no baseDir is attached the token passes through unsubstituted. A `references/*.md` READ AT RUN TIME is not definition text, so the token arrives literally and names nothing -- CONFIRMED BEHAVIOURALLY (peer harness run, container fidelity, sonnet-5): one skill carrying the same token in SKILL.md and in references/paths.md delivered `BODY_PATH=/sessions/.../scripts/y.py` substituted and `SCRIPT_PATH=${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/y.py` literal, read from the DELIVERED content in the event stream rather than the model's report (which rules out the model expanding it itself from a path it had read). **COMMANDS ARE ALSO EXCLUDED, and this is the easy one to get wrong.** Both replacement sites in the `bz` builder are guarded on `g.isSkillMode`, whose default is FALSE; the two command load sites pass it explicitly false (`FAt(T.commandsPath, ..., {isSkillMode:!1})` -> 'Loaded N commands'), while skills pass true (`bz(..., {isSkillMode:!0})` with `pe.baseDir`). So a `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}` in a command file arrives literally, exactly as in a reference file. THE TRAP: the very next statement substitutes ${CLAUDE_SESSION_ID} and ${CLAUDE_EFFORT} OUTSIDE that guard, so commands ARE a substituting definition surface -- just not for this token. Asking 'does substitution happen in commands?' returns yes and gives the wrong answer. The correct scope is the SKILL.md body and its `allowed-tools`, and nothing else. Caveat: a SECOND builder gates on a truthy `baseDir` rather than the flag; its call sites are untraced here, so a path where a command acquires a baseDir is not ruled out. The same load-time pass substitutes ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}, ${CLAUDE_SESSION_ID} and ${CLAUDE_EFFORT}, and prepends `Base directory for this skill: <abs path>` -- the skill's own root is legible to the MODEL in body text and to nothing else. WHY IT MATTERS: this is the token skill authors reach for first, and it had no registry entry of its own while CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT was hardened across three passes -- the recommended variable was the undocumented one. SCOPE: read first-party from the CLI 2.1.250 extracted bundle -- 6 occurrences, of which 4 are replacement CALL SITES (two getPromptForCommand body-text paths, two `allowed-tools` paths) and 2 are string-table entries. A first write of this entry said 'five substitution sites', from a Python context-window pass whose 260-char windows merged two adjacent hits; `grep -a -o` gives the true 6. CROSS-VERSION: the same 4-call-sites + 2-string-table split was independently enumerated by byte offset in the CLI 2.1.251 bundle by a peer session -- a DIFFERENT build, though on the same machine, so this is two artifacts and one host, not independent replication. The two string-table entries sit adjacent to `Base directory for this skill:`, ${CLAUDE_SESSION_ID} and ${CLAUDE_EFFORT} -- interned constants of the same substitution family, not additional exports. INSTRUMENT NOTE: plain `grep`/`grep -o`/`grep -c` return NOTHING on this bundle -- grep classifies it as binary and declines silently, printing no 'Binary file matches' line when counting, so a refusal is indistinguishable from a zero. Use `grep -a`. A positive control (a token known to be present) catches it; `-a` prevents it.

entries.name: LocalSessions / LocalAgentModeSessions (effort + extended-thinking methods)
entries.summary: setEffort/setExtendedThinking (also on LocalAgentModeSessions)/getEffort/getDefaultEffort/setFastMode. Spawn-time resolution is settings-file-driven, NOT CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL-backed (corrects L114): effort = qgi(effortOverride, A1e(model)=settings.effortByModel[model], E2t()=settings.effort||"medium"); extended thinking = zgi(enabled, override, killSwitch) yielding maxThinkingTokens strictly 31999 or 0 (NX=31999), never an arbitrary budget. Four per-model effort classes: literal picker models (s1r map), no-picker models (still emit --effort medium), fable/mythos regex-default class (o1r/i1r, disallowThinkingDisabled:true), unknown models (no config). Delivered exclusively as CLI flags (--effort <level>, --max-thinking-tokens <N> / --thinking disabled); CLAUDE_EFFORT and MAX_THINKING_TOKENS are no-ops as INBOUND env vars at spawn (nothing reads them); note CLAUDE_EFFORT is nonetheless exported OUTBOUND to Bash/hook children -- see env.CLAUDE_EFFORT. Live-session setEffort calls query.applyFlagSettings({effortLevel}); live-session setExtendedThinking calls query.setMaxThinkingTokens(enabled?31999:0) -- first concrete payload shapes for the apply_flag_settings / set_max_thinking_tokens control-protocol subtypes. entries.name: Task
entries.summary: Subagent dispatch. Input schema (THm/SHm/fLo): description, prompt, subagent_type, model, run_in_background, name, team_name (deprecated), mode, isolation, cwd -- NO resume parameter; every call spawns a fresh agent (tengu_agent_tool_selected is_resume:false). run_in_background is omitted from the schema when CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS is set or the fork experiment (PX()) is active; cwd is always omitted model-facing (Task input schema .omit({cwd:!0})). Continuation lives elsewhere: SendMessage resume (tool.SendMessage), subagent_type 'fork' (inherits full conversation context), Workflow resumeFromRunId. Type-less dispatch (subagent_type omitted) falls back to the built-in general-purpose type with tools:["*"] -- the FULL wildcard tool surface, including mcp__workspace__bash in Cowork host-loop; production audit-log evidence shows this fallback firing routinely (113 of 509 real dispatches across 39 sessions on one machine carried no subagent_type at all). Depth cap 5 (NMr host / BLr in-VM), enforced by hiding the Agent/Task tool itself from a sub-agent's own composed toolset once agentDepth>=5; no Task-specific fan-out/concurrency cap exists anywhere in either binary -- the only bound on parallel sub-agent starts is the generic env.CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_TOOL_USE_CONCURRENCY scheduler window.

provenance.note: type-less dispatch general-purpose fallback + depth cap + no fan-out cap, confirmed with production audit-log evidence

entries.name: plugin bin/ on the Bash tool's PATH
entries.summary: UNDOCUMENTED AFFORDANCE (Ch48/L173). Z$n() maps every ENABLED, NON-BUILTIN plugin with a path to <path>/bin and adds it to the Bash tool's PATH, dropping any path matching /[:"'$`\\\n\r]/ SILENTLY (log line only). Measured live in three lanes, each namespace-correct for its own shell: standalone CLI ~/.claude/plugins/cache/<mp>/<plugin>/<ver>/bin (35 entries, ZERO existed); Cowork host-loop VM shell /sessions/<slug>/mnt/.remote-plugins/plugin_<id>/bin (1 entry, EXISTS, populated with a 54-byte read-only executable); Cowork cloud /root/.claude/plugins/synced/<orgUuid>_<accountUuid>/<plugin>/bin (20 entries). THE ASYMMETRY: in ONE host-loop session CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT resolves to a HOST path the VM shell cannot use while the bin PATH entry resolves to a VM path it can -- so a bin/ launcher is the only measured channel giving a plugin its root in the shell's own namespace, and PATH lookup means no path crosses the boundary. Functionally verified: a bare command resolved and cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd returned the plugin root. CAVEATS: a PATH entry is NOT evidence the dir exists -- Z$n() performs NO existence check, so the entry count is a fact about the ENABLED-PLUGIN COUNT and says nothing about disk (RETRACTED 2026-08-29: this caveat previously read 'bin/ is provisioned by sync/install, not carried in plugin source', inferred from 35-entries/0-directories; a source-committed bin/ DOES survive install byte-identically, install narrowing the mode 755->700 while the execute bit survives). ORG-REMOTE LANE HAS A SECOND WRITER: across all 26 org-remote plugin roots on one machine, bin/ exists IFF the manifest declares `clis`, and the launcher's filename equals the declared CLI key (25 without, 1 with, 0 violations) -- the runtime materialises `exec -a "$0" /opt/cowork/cli-wrapper "$@"` shims there, so declaring clis:{foo:...} means the runtime owns bin/foo; do not ship a launcher by that name. Whether a differently-named authored launcher survives re-provisioning is UNTESTED. Also: the Cowork mount is read-only; metacharacter paths vanish with no model-visible error. Version floor UNVERIFIED -- the embedded CHANGELOG reaches only 2.1.220.
